newsitem.title: THAILAND: Unocal begins Andaman Sea exploration.
newsitem.headline: Unocal begins Andaman Sea exploration.

text.p: Unocal Bangkok, a unit of U.S.-based Unocal Corp, on Thursday announced the start of its exploration for petroleum in the Andaman Sea under a six-year programme with a budget of 1.2 billion baht ($48 million).
Unocal found some natural gas in this area in a search during the 1970s, but relinquished the concession due to a limited market for it at the time, a company official said.
A seismic geophysical survey will be done at the two concession blocks, W8/38 and W9/38, which were awarded in June by the Industry Ministry to a Unocal-led consortium.
The consortium comprised Unocal Bangkok, Statoil Siam, a unit of Statoil, and Total Korat, a unit of France-based Total SA, the official said.

The group will use deep water exploration technology with the blocks which are some 100 to 250 km (60-150 miles) off the coast of southern Phuket province. Two exploration wells are planned for late 1997.

Unocal is currently operator for nine fields in the Gulf of Thailand, with an average gas production rate of 760 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd). The rate is expected to rise to 1,000 mmcfd in 1997, the official said.
